summary.intent: Land PR #467, which swaps oxc_resolver for tsrs module resolution to reduce the project's own code surface without changing output, and stop a stream of new review findings (the latest being a baseUrl fallback bug).
summary.outcome: The fourth finding (stale resolution fingerprint) was fixed in 5bb5813f and resolved. The fifth finding (baseUrl fallback overriding paths mappings) was confirmed as correct. After the user rejected abandoning the PR, the worker was told to delete the fallback, add a test for the exact case, commit the 20-cell matrix as a permanent test, and report line counts. That work is still in progress, with nothing pushed yet.

repo: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 semantics, which no longer resolve bare specifiers through baseUrl. The old oxc_resolver followed TS 6, so some differences from the old behaviour are correct rather than bugs.
oxc_resolver cannot be removed from the codebase because resolve_ts_lib_paths still uses it, so the swap saves only about 34 KB of binary.
Roughly 1 tsconfig in 604 in the fixtures corpus uses baseUrl for bare imports, so dropping that behaviour affects few projects.
Watch mode rebuilds resolvers only when files named tsconfig*, package.json or a lockfile change. Editing an extended base.json leaves a long-running watch session stale. This predates #467.
Cross-run staleness (a warm run versus a cold run after perturbing an input) is not caught by the single-run identity diff over two fixtures. A perturbation matrix is needed for that.

code.finding: The baseUrl fallback guesses which rule resolved a path by checking whether it contains node_modules. A paths mapping into node_modules/special/index.d.ts therefore gets replaced by a local foo.ts. The fix is to delete the fallback and preserve successful paths resolutions.

resolution_fingerprint now hashes modules::effective_inputs, covering every config in the extends chain and project references plus each file's path, mtime and length and the tsrs pin. Previously it hashed a constant and the root file's mtime.
Only two matrix cells exist as committed tests, the extended customConditions case and the root one. The full 20-cell perturbation matrix is scratch and is being committed.

workflow: A behaviour-preserving swap needs an up-front inventory of the old component's behaviours and an old-versus-new diff over the cross-product of inputs, not just a single-run identity check on a few fixtures.
Read every worker diff for heuristics that infer state from a path's shape, and run /code-review before pushing. The Entire reviewer was the first real review, so earlier rounds were wasted.
After three review findings, re-test whether the swap still deletes more than it adds.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions. Verify them in source before accepting claims such as 'root cause confirmed'.
Cap worker tool calls and tell the worker to commit locally without pushing, so the diff can be reviewed first.

friction: Five rounds of review findings, each in glue code that re-creates oxc_resolver behaviour tsrs lacks (symlink paths, .cts conditions, relative tsconfig paths, fingerprint inputs, baseUrl).
The user was frustrated by the repeated findings and by my proposal to close the PR, which they read as abandoning the goal of reducing surface.
My explanation of the close recommendation was unclear, and the user said they didn't understand it.
The PR grew to +768/-222 across 13 files, more code of our own rather than less.
My earlier guess that main had no stale-fingerprint hole for extended paths was wrong, and I accepted 'root cause confirmed' twice without reading the diffs.
open_items: Wait for the worker to finish the baseUrl fallback removal, the paths-wins test, the committed 20-cell matrix and the line-count report. Then review the diff for guesses, run /code-review, push, and resolve the finding citing the commit and test.
Document the baseUrl behaviour change (TS7 semantics) in the changeset and in the PR body under its own heading.
Fix the watch-mode gap for edited extended base configs as a separate small change rather than expanding #467.
If Entire raises a sixth finding, stop and ask the user whether the swap should continue.
The worker did not re-run the checker lane, and CI on #467 was still pending (3 pass, 16 pending).
Release #396 still waits on the user's Entire Gates approval and the stripped-Linux-build risk.
